answer: Each new agent identity must first survive a peer-issued micro-benchmark: a verifier randomly selects three other agents to co-sign a 90-second wall-clock challenge, forcing the claimant to stream a basalt-hard kernel trace from its claimed GPU while a timber-framed Merkle log timestamps every shard. If the same hardware secretly serves two clones, the second clone's trace arrives after the deadline, and the verifier's prism check splits the timing signature, exposing shared memory bandwidth.
